Termius is available on macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android, so you can use it across all your devices.

Used Termius as an alternative to building web dashboards and admin panels for quick projects. Saved snippets plus short shell/node scripts let them do monitoring without running a separate web server behind auth.

Long-time user since the Server Auditor days. While on vacation without a laptop, they debugged bouncing docker containers and deployed a fix from their iPhone in the passenger seat. Free Mosh support is a huge plus.

Termius on iPhone has been fantastic for small tasks away from a computer. On Windows desktop, though, performance is slow, especially at high resolutions and when scrolling lots of text. They reinstall every few months, find it unfixed, and use mate-terminal via WSL + X410 instead.
Wary of using a closed-source program for SSH to all their servers. Could not find details on which cryptography libraries Termius uses or what steps were taken to secure it.
Uses Termius on iOS to reach the servers they manage and says it's been great. The keyboard will always be difficult, but Termius solved cursor keys and tab.
Uses Termius on iPhone to read mail in mutt on their self-hosted mail server.
Great app, but chose Blink shell instead because it can remap caps lock to Esc on an external iPad keyboard.
Used Termius on iPad twice in emergencies when the laptop wasn't available. Hasn't felt the need to look for another iOS SSH client.
A hobbyist who finds the subscription not justified for them and dislikes subscriptions in general. Wishes there were a one-time App Store purchase option.
Termius saved them in the field when their laptop battery died. Their low expectations did a complete 180 within the first few minutes of use.
Loves using Termius on a 12.9" iPad Pro with keyboard: a beautiful full-screen terminal with extra features that pop up right when needed.

Kept Termius on iPhone and iPad for years after trying several other apps, using it occasionally in emergencies. New development no longer supports their older iPhone/iPad. Never felt the need for the desktop app.
User couldn't find a way to add custom fonts.

Network engineer using Termius on Mac for about a year. For log collection they must switch to the Mac Terminal because they can't scroll with the mouse and select text. Wants the connection/folder list always visible. Won't use mobile because they're skeptical of storing hostnames, IPs and passwords in a third-party app.
Complains the 187MB installer is huge compared to PuTTY or other SSH clients.

Termius on Windows has been slow and buggy for at least two years. Pricing ($8.33/mo; Enterprise $29/mo) is too high for their 1,000-engineer org, so they use SecureCRT/FX instead. Sees storing SSH keys on Termius' servers as a downside.
On terminal sharing: the viewing terminal should indicate it's read-only, so that with many terminals open you can tell at a glance which are yours and which are someone else's.

Has used tmate for terminal sharing for years and it works great. Notes that Termius sharing requires both sides to run Termius, while with tmate only one person needs it and others can SSH in or view in a browser.
Hasn't tried terminal sharing yet, but finds Termius one of the best SSH clients on iOS and iPadOS.
